package_info.why_malicious: The analyzed artifacts deliver and execute well-known malware (Zeus Sphinx banking trojan, FIN7 infection chain, Magecart skimmer) via multiple vectors (malicious macros, USB HID emulation, injected JavaScript), enabling credential theft, banking fraud, and payment data exfiltration. These behaviors are highly malicious, leveraging social engineering and technical exploits to compromise victims.

execution_context.file_location: malicious macro in Word document attached to phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
AutoOpen()
  ' Malicious macro code here
  ' Downloads and executes Zeus Sphinx payload
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the Word document and enables macros, the macro executes, downloads the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan from a remote server, and runs it on the victim's machine, resulting in credential theft and potential banking fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros in unsolicited Office documents that download and execute binaries are a classic and highly effective malware delivery technique, often used in targeted phishing attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Word documents should not contain macros that initiate network connections or execute external code without explicit user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation uses macros to fetch data or automate document processing, but never to download and execute untrusted binaries from the internet.
key_indicators: Macro triggers automatically on document open
Initiates download of executable payload from remote server
Executes downloaded code without user consent
Presence of password-protected document with embedded macro

execution_context.file_location: PowerShell command executed via HID emulation from USB device

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon USB device insertion, the device emulates keyboard input to launch PowerShell, which downloads and executes a remote script from a malicious server, initiating the FIN7 infection chain and compromising the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: USB devices that emulate keyboard input to execute PowerShell commands are a well-documented malware delivery vector, often bypassing traditional endpoint protections.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal USB devices should not inject keystrokes to launch PowerShell or download and execute remote scripts without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate USB devices may automate setup or configuration, but never to download and execute untrusted remote scripts.
key_indicators: PowerShell process launched via HID/keyboard emulation
Remote script downloaded and executed from external domain
No user interaction required for code execution
Unusual PowerShell activity immediately after USB insertion

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits a payment form on the checkout page, the injected JavaScript intercepts the credit card data and exfiltrates it via a POST request to a remote attacker-controlled server, resulting in payment data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data from checkout pages is a hallmark of Magecart and similar web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts on payment pages should never send sensitive payment data to unknown or third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Payment processors may send data to their own secure servers, but not to unrecognized or attacker-controlled domains.
key_indicators: Form data exfiltration to external, non-payment domain
Injected or unauthorized JavaScript present on payment page
No user awareness or consent for data transmission
Network requests to domains unrelated to legitimate payment processing

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with password-protected Word document containing a malicious macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of macro and download of Zeus Sphinx trojan

attack_chain.action: User opens the document and enables macros, triggering the download and execution of the banking trojan.
Victim receives a USB device in the mail, which emulates keyboard input to launch PowerShell and download malware.
Malicious JavaScript is injected into e-commerce checkout pages, skimming credit card data at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of payment data to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Office macros that initiate network connections and download or execute binaries upon document open
PowerShell processes launched via HID/keyboard emulation from USB devices, especially immediately after device insertion
JavaScript injected into payment or checkout pages that exfiltrates form data to external, non-payment domains
file_indicators: Password-protected Word documents with embedded macros
Unexpected PowerShell execution events following USB device insertion
Presence of unauthorized or modified JavaScript files on e-commerce checkout pages
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known malware C2 domains (e.g., Zeus Sphinx, FIN7, Magecart infrastructure)
POST requests from browser sessions on checkout pages to unrecognized or suspicious external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that initiate network connections or drop executables. Detect PowerShell processes launched shortly after USB device insertion, especially those that download and execute remote scripts. Inspect e-commerce sites for unauthorized JavaScript that sends payment data to external domains. Use network monitoring to flag suspicious outbound connections to known malicious infrastructure and POST requests from checkout pages to non-payment domains.
